title: SEO & Authority Content Lead
description: What ranks in two years matters more than what publishes this week. A short pitch for who this is: You play the long game. You've watched a single well-built piece quietly drive traffic for years. You've also watched companies torch their search presence by pumping out AI-generated noise because someone read a thread about content velocity. You don't confuse output with strategy. You can pull up a SERP and explain, page by page, what each ranking result is doing well and where the gap is. You think most "SEO advice" online is recycled and shallow, and you can argue why. ABOUT SGEN SGEN doesn't yet have authority in search. Somebody Googling "WordPress alternative for agencies" in 2027 should land on a SGEN piece that's actually useful — not keyword bait. Somebody Googling "why Elementor sites are slow" should find a piece that explains the cause honestly and only mentions SGEN where the mention earns it. Somebody Googling "headless vs full-stack CMS" should find a comparison that reads like it was written by someone who's built both. That's the work — building the search-and-authority layer that compounds over years, not months. WHO FITS You've done patient SEO before. The kind that takes 9–12 months to show its full effect and then stays for years. You know the difference between a topic cluster and a content calendar. You can talk through search intent, internal linking, and E-E-A-T without sounding like you got it off a Twitter thread. You treat Ahrefs and Semrush as inputs, not gospel. You can read three paragraphs of a piece and tell whether the writer actually knows the subject. You'd rather publish ten strong pieces a year than fifty mediocre ones. HAVE A REAL TAKE ON CONTENT STRATEGY You probably have strong opinions about most B2B SaaS blogs. The 5-reasons posts. The 4,000-word ultimate guides that say almost nothing. The AI-generated round-ups that age in weeks. You can articulate why most company blogs underperform: too much volume, too little point of view, no internal-link architecture, no respect for the reader's time. You believe quality compounds and volume decays — and you can back it with examples from work you've done. STEADY THROUGH SLOW MONTHS Some pieces won't rank for months. Some will spike at six. Some will get quietly large a year after publishing. You don't panic at month-one numbers. You don't pivot the strategy after one flop. You measure, wait, revise, re-link, and let the work do its job. Search authority is a long conversation. You're comfortable in long conversations. THE ACTUAL WORK Topic strategy. Map the keyword and concept universe SGEN should own — WordPress alternatives, modern CMS, agency tooling, hosting-plus-builder-plus-CMS as one platform. Cluster it. Sequence it. Build a 12-month plan, not a 30-day calendar. Long-form pieces. Write or commission the deep posts — pillar articles, honest comparisons, technical explainers, opinion-led essays. The ones that get cited, linked to, and quoted in newsletters. Voice support from Jerome; distribution support from the Growth Marketer. Comparison pages. SGEN vs. WordPress. SGEN vs. Webflow. SGEN vs. Framer. SGEN vs. Squarespace. Real comparisons that acknowledge where SGEN isn't the right answer. That honesty is what makes the rest of the page credible. Internal architecture. Design how the content links to itself. Keep the structure clean. Prevent the sprawl that wrecks most company blogs after year two. Editorial bar. Set the quality standard for the blog and enforce it. Lighter, faster posts from the Growth Marketer are welcome on their own lane; the authority pieces all run through you. Measurement. Organic traffic by cluster, rank position on target queries, organic backlinks, pieces that worked and didn't. Monthly read-out, honest, no vanity metrics. WHAT WE’RE CHECKING FOR - A portfolio with rankings. Pieces you wrote that ranked or drove traffic. If you can talk through why they worked, even better. - English that reads native. Long pieces have to hold the reader. Every paragraph earns its place. - WordPress and adjacent-CMS literacy. You don't need to be a developer. You need enough fluency in the ecosystem — plugins, builders, hosts, the actual pain — to write about it credibly. Webflow, Framer, Ghost, Shopify experience is a plus. - SEO that isn't tricks. Topic clusters, intent, internal linking, durable on-page. You can also explain why most public SEO advice is shallow. - A track record of compounding work. A small number of pieces still driving traffic years after publishing beats a large number that stopped working in three months. - Sustainable cadence. One serious piece every two weeks, at this length, at this depth. Not faster. Not slower. PROBABLY YOU IF - You can name three SaaS blogs you respect and three you consider noise — with reasoning for each. - You've personally written a piece still ranking a year later. - You've watched a content program fail because somebody confused "publish more" with "build authority." - You've rewritten an old post and watched its traffic multiply. - You think most AI content is going to age poorly, and you can say why. - You enjoy reading SERPs. WHAT THIS ISN’T It isn't a content mill. It isn't four AI-assisted posts a week. It isn't repackaging the docs as blog posts. It isn't competitor comparisons where SGEN always wins. It's a long-horizon search strategy run by somebody who's done it before and has the receipts. WHY IT MATTERS Search is the most durable acquisition channel a software company has access to. Communities shift. Algorithms change. Ads get expensive. A piece that ranks on a high-intent query, with real depth and an honest point of view, keeps working for years. The right hire here plants the pieces that quietly carry SGEN's growth long after they shipped. The wrong hire here publishes volume that ranks for nothing. COMPENSATION $600-$650 USD per month SCHEDULE - 8 hour shift, Monday to Friday, 7:00AM to 4:00PM Philippine Time. - Minimal overtime during weekdays and weekends will be expected as part of salary SGEN is proud to be an equal opportunity employer committed to a diverse and inclusive work environment. All qualified applicants will receive consideration for employment without regard to race, color, religion, sex, sexual orientation, gender identity or expression, national origin, marital status, disability, veteran status or any other basis protected by law. You care about the viewer's experience. You enjoy continuous improvement and are always looking for ways to make each project better than the last. Required Qualifications To be considered, you should have: Professional experience editing long-form video content Experience producing educational or course-based content Advanced proficiency with Adobe Premiere Pro Working knowledge of Adobe After Effects Strong understanding of motion graphics Experience with color correction and audio editing Excellent organizational skills Ability to manage multiple projects simultaneously Strong English comprehension Reliable high-speed internet A professional remote workspace Ability to work full-time during U.S. Eastern Time business hours Preferred Qualifications While not required, these are considered major advantages: Experience editing online learning platforms Experience creating e-learning courses Motion graphics experience Adobe Creative Cloud proficiency ---------- or collaborative review workflow experience Experience working with large content libraries Podcast editing experience Documentary-style storytelling experience Experience editing business or leadership education What Makes This Position Different This isn't a freelance contract. This isn't project-based work. This is a full-time career opportunity. Our post-production department currently consists of six talented professionals who work together every day to produce some of the highest-quality educational content in our industry. Most members of our creative team remain with Pest Daily for years. We invest heavily in our people because we believe great teams create great work. If you're looking for a company where you can grow professionally, collaborate with talented creatives, and build a long-term career, this is an opportunity worth considering. We work with a dedicated fulfillment partner (DayOne) and an external advertising agency  running Google Shopping at scale. Our volume sits at 100+ disputes per week across Shopify Payments, PayPal, and Whop, plus daily supplier coordination, customer service oversight, and agency communication via Slack. We're not a side hustle. This is a serious operation, and we're building it like one. What we're hiring for: We're looking for a Backend Operations Manager — a true A-player who can take the operational weight off the founder's shoulders. You will own the day-to-day backend of the business: disputes, chargebacks, supply chain, customer service, and partner communication. If you've ever felt like you were carrying a whole company on your back and want a place that rewards that — we want to talk. What you'll own (of course, we have teams with employees and managers in each department, but you will be ultimately responsible for all departments): Disputes & Chargebacks (~40% of role) * Manage 100+ disputes per week across Shopify Payments, PayPal, and Whop * Build and execute evidence packages following our internal SOPs * Track win rates per processor, per store, per reason code * Identify patterns (fraud rings, recurring chargeback reasons) and flag them upstream * Coordinate with PayPal/Stripe support when escalations are needed Supply Chain & Supplier Coordination (~25%) * Daily communication with our fulfillment partner (DayOne) via Slack * Verify supplier invoices against our internal quote sheet (Empire X DayOne) * Flag discrepancies, missing SKUs, pricing mismatches * Track shipping issues, lost packages, returns * Coordinate inventory questions across multiple stores/entities Customer Service Oversight (~20%) * Manage CS workflows across our store portfolio * Handle escalations that frontline agents can't resolve * Spot recurring issues and turn them into process improvements * Keep response-time SLAs in check Who you are This is a backend manager role, not a VA role. We're looking for someone who: - Has run operations for multi-store Shopify or DTC businesses before (not just one store) - Has serious experience with PayPal disputes and Shopify Payments chargebacks at volume — you know what "compelling evidence" actually means and which arguments win - Has worked with fulfillment partners and knows how to read an invoice critically - Communicates in clear, professional English — written and spoken - Lives in Slack comfortably and can hold structured conversations across multiple channels - Is proactive — you don't wait to be told what to do, you spot problems and propose fixes - Is calm under volume — 100+ disputes a week doesn't faze you - Owns outcomes, not tasks Must-haves: - 3+ years managing operations for an e-commerce business (Shopify preferred) - Hands-on experience defending chargebacks (Shopify Payments AND PayPal — not just one) - Comfortable working with multiple legal entities, multiple stores, multiple payment processors - Excellent written English - Self-managed — full-time available, reliable internet, professional setup - Available full-time (50 hrs/week), long-term commitment Nice-to-haves + Experience with Whop disputes + Familiarity with Google Shopping feeds (Simprosys, Multifeeds, Pythago) + Experience working with external ad agencies + Background in fashion / branded DTC + Process documentation experience (writing SOPs, training others) + Comfort working with AI tools (we're heavily AI-augmented and will give you serious AI leverage) What we offer: + Long-term, full-time role — we're hiring for years, not weeks + Competitive rate based on experience (range: $12–20/hr, open to higher for the right person) + Real ownership — you'll be the backend, not just a task-taker + AI leverage — we build AI agents to do the repetitive work so you can focus on judgment calls + Growth path — as we scale to 50+ stores and a $100M brand portfolio, this role grows with us + Direct access to the founder — no middle layers, no politics, no nonsense How to apply We get a lot of templated applications. Here's how to make sure we read yours: Start your cover letter with the word "EMPIRE" so we know you actually read this post. Then, in your application, briefly tell us: - How many Shopify stores have you managed simultaneously, and which payment processors did they use? - What's the highest dispute/chargeback volume you've handled in a single week? What was your win rate? - Tell us about a time you caught a supplier invoice error. What was the discrepancy and how much did you save? - What's your timezone, and what hours can you commit to overlapping with CET (Netherlands)? - Why this role specifically — what about it fits where you want to go in the next 2–3 years? Applications without these answers will not be reviewed.

title: Real Estate Research Assistant
description: About the Role •We are looking for a detail-oriented property researcher to help identify land parcels in the United States that may fit specific acquisition criteria. •This role requires strong web research skills, comfort using county GIS maps, attention to zoning and parcel details, and accurate Excel or Google Sheets work. •You  need to be reliable, organized, and able to follow detailed instructions. Primary Responsibilities •Research land parcels using LandID, county GIS maps, assessor records, property appraiser websites, zoning maps, planning department websites, and other public sources. (I will teach how to use LandID software if you have not used it). •Identify parcels that match specific search criteria such as acreage, zoning, road access, topography, wetlands, nearby development, utilities, and current listing status. •Enter parcel data into Excel or Google Sheets using a required format. •Record parcel number, owner name, owner mailing address, site address, acreage, zoning, land use, road access, nearby projects, notes, and source links. •Review GIS maps to check parcel boundaries, roads, nearby subdivisions, utilities, floodplain/wetland indicators, and surrounding development patterns. •Check whether a property appears to be currently listed for sale and exclude listed properties when instructed. •Organize findings clearly so another person can quickly verify the parcel. •Flag uncertain items instead of guessing. Required Skills •Strong Excel or Google Sheets skills, including sorting, filtering, formatting, hyperlinks, and clean data entry. •Ability to use online GIS maps and parcel viewers. •Ability to research zoning and land use information from county or city websites. •Strong attention to detail and accuracy. •Comfort working with U.S. property records and public data websites. •Ability to follow written instructions exactly. •Good written English for notes, summaries, and questions. •Reliable internet connection and ability to meet deadlines. Helpful Experience •Real estate research, land research, title research, GIS research, zoning research, or property data entry. •Experience with county assessor websites, planning and zoning maps, GIS parcel viewers, Google Earth, FEMA maps, or listing websites. •Experience researching agricultural land, development land, vacant land, or residential growth areas. •Experience checking roads, utilities, wetlands, floodplain, slope, and nearby residential development. Typical Parcel Criteria You May Research •20 or more acres. •Relatively flat land or limited topographical change. •At least two possible road access points when available. •No major wetlands on the usable portion of the property. •Agricultural, rural residential, transition, or similar zoning. •Near existing development or active residential building projects. •Near water, sewer, or other utility infrastructure when possible. •Not currently listed for sale, unless instructed otherwise. •Owner mailing address available from public records when possible. Work Product Expected •A clean Excel or Google Sheets file with one parcel per row. •Boundary marking for each parcel inside LandID software •Clear flags for anything uncertain or needing review. •Screenshots or map links when requested. Quality Standards •Accuracy matters more than speed. •Do not guess. Mark uncertain information as uncertain. •Keep spreadsheet formatting clean and consistent. •Do not include parcels that clearly fail the criteria. •Ask questions early if instructions are unclear. Paid Test Project •The first assignment will be a paid test project. •You will be given one search area and a spreadsheet template. •The goal is to find a small number of qualified parcels and show that your research is accurate, organized, and easy to verify. •Strong performance on the test project may lead to ongoing work.

description: What You Will Be Doing You will be producing 10-15 short-form videos per day (25-120 seconds each) for health and wellness pages on Instagram and Facebook . Every morning, you receive a Google Drive folder for each reel — it includes a full production file (every image prompt, video prompt, and dialogue line already written) plus all the reference images you need. Your job is to follow it and turn it into a polished, ready-to-post vertical reel using AI tools and CapCut Pro. This is a production role — 95% of it is execution. You do not write scripts. You do not make creative decisions about content. The only creative judgment you make is ensuring visual continuity from scene to scene — backgrounds, props, wardrobe, and prop placement should flow naturally as the video progresses. If a clip breaks continuity (wrong background, prop disappears, character looks different), you regenerate or adjust. Spotting these is the single most important skill — the difference between a video that gets 10k views and one that gets 100k. The Video Style You Will Produce Full Avatar + B-Roll Cuts. The AI character takes up most of the screen and speaks directly to camera. The video cuts to AI-generated b-roll ---------- nts at key points in the script. Captions and overlays appear throughout. This is the style used for personal, authority-building wellness content. Each production file tells you exactly which scenes need character vs b-roll, and includes the exact image prompts and video prompts for each scene. Tools You Need To Have (required to apply) - Google AI Pro OR Google AI Ultra subscription - CapCut Pro subscription Tools I Provide (after signing) - ElevenLabs — Generate AI voice for select reels using the cloned voice I provide (used on roughly 1 in 4 reels — the rest use the voice built into Veo 3.1) - Veo 3.1 — Turn images into ~8 second video clips with voice - Google Gemini Ultra account — Flow image generation + higher rate limits - Nano Banana Pro — High-quality reference images - Google Drive — Receive production folders, deliver finished videos I will train you on the exact workflow for each tool. Previous experience is a plus but not required — what matters is your ability to learn fast and follow detailed instructions. Basic Editing Skills Needed - Stitching multiple 8-second Veo clips into one coherent video - Spotting visual continuity breaks and fixing them - Adding accurate captions - Cutting dead space, tightening pacing - Minor effects: dynamic zoom, transitions, overlays - Attention to timing and pacing — small details separate viral content from average content Requirements - Active Google AI Pro or Ultra subscription (required) - Active CapCut Pro subscription (required) - Strong CapCut / video editing skills (you must demonstrate this in the recreate assignments below) - Excellent English reading comprehension — production files are detailed and must be followed precisely - Extremely detail-oriented - Reliable, fast internet connection - Available 6-8 hours per day, 5-6 days per week (consistency matters more than fixed hours) - PH timezone or similar - Can receive payments via PayPal - Comfortable learning AI tools (I will train you, but you must be a fast and eager learner) - Good at taking direct feedback and improving fast Pay - Starting: $400/month - Performance raise: $500+/month once you are consistently producing high-quality videos at speed - Big bonuses when content performs well ($50 per 1 million views) - Payment via PayPal, monthly - This is a long-term position. I am building a content network and need someone who can grow with it. The Bigger Picture This is my first VA hire. I am building a content network across multiple wellness brands and I need someone who can grow with me, not just clock hours. The right person here has a clear path to: - $1,000+/month earnings as output and quality scale - A manager role training the next VAs I hire — once you have the workflow locked, you teach it - Real input into how my team operates, what we systemize, what we build next If you want a paycheck only, this is not the role for you. If you want to plant a flag and grow with an operator who is moving fast, this is rare and I will know it when I see it. How to Apply — Two-Stage Recreate Process + Interview Call To apply, you must complete a two-stage recreate process so I can evaluate your skills. This replaces a traditional interview — your work speaks for itself. You will use your own Google AI Pro/Ultra account and your own CapCut Pro throughout. Stage 1 — Recreate 1: Exact Reproduction I will send you: - A reel from my own account - The single reference image I used to make it Your task: Recreate the video as exactly as you can. Match the Nano Banana Pro image generations, the cuts, the editing, and the voice. I want to see your best attempt at reverse-engineering my style. You have 24 hours from receiving the materials to submit via Google Drive: - The finished video (mp4) - A Google Doc with every prompt you wrote — the image prompts AND the Veo prompts. I want to see your thinking, not just the output. - 2-3 sentences on your process: what you noticed about the original, what was hard, what you'd improve. This tests your ability to study a video, reverse-engineer it, and write the prompts that produce something close. This is the most important part of the application. I will review and respond within 24-48 hours. Stage 2 — Recreate 2: Independent Production (only if Recreate 1 is approved) If your Recreate 1 looks strong, I will approve you to move on and send you a production file with all prompts already written. Your task: Produce the complete video from the file. No tutorial, no walkthrough — just execute. You have 24 hours from receiving the materials to submit via Google Drive: - The finished video (mp4) This tests your ability to read a production file and turn it into a polished reel — which is exactly what you will do every day in this role. Stage 3 — The Call If both recreates look strong, we hop on a 15 to 30-minute video call. I will walk you through my full workflow live — exactly how I produce these videos — so you understand what you are signing up for. You will have time to ask me anything and tell me why you would be a great fit. This is how I make the final decision. To Apply, Send a Message With: - Confirmation that you have an active Google AI Pro or Ultra subscription AND an active CapCut Pro subscription - Your CapCut / video editing experience (specific examples, portfolio links, or a brief description of what you have edited before) - Any experience with AI tools (Veo, Google Flow, Nano Banana, ElevenLabs, HeyGen, Kling, etc.) — even minimal - Your availability (hours per day, days per week, timezone) - One paragraph on why you would be a great fit for this role - Confirming you will deliver Recreate 1 within 24 hours of receiving the materials, and Recreate 2 within 24 hours of approval to move on I will respond within 12 hours of your application with the Recreate 1 materials. This is a production role, not a creative role. If you thrive on following clear systems, delivering consistent quality, and getting better every day, this is for you.

title: Systems & Automation Specialist (No-Code Workflows)
description: **Part-time. Remote. Clay, Notion, reporting, and automations.** --- ## The short version I run a small agency. There's a lot going on behind the client work. Lead lists, outreach, reporting, internal tools, automations. I build most of it myself right now. I've got to the point where I need someone to own it. This is not an admin or VA role. I need someone who thinks in systems. You look at a process and work it out. When this happens here, that should happen there. And it stays clean while it does. Do you like taking a messy workflow and making it simple? Then this is a good fit. --- ## What the role is Most of the work is "if this, then that" logic across tools. You also keep the data behind it clean. A lot of it looks like this. We take raw data. We run it through a chain of checks and steps. We clean it as it goes. Then we send each record to the right place on its own. That's one system. There are more like it. There's the Notion side too, which keeps the work in order. And the reporting side, which keeps the numbers honest. Here's the key part. This is a build role, not a run role. I've got people who run the day to day. The reports, the outreach, the uploads. What I'm missing is someone who owns the systems under all of that. You design them. You automate them. You fix them when they break. You make them simpler so the team moves faster. You build the machine. You don't turn the handle on it each day. You don't need to know every tool I use. You need to be the type who can open a new one and work out the logic. That counts more than any tool on your CV. --- ## What you'd be doing The work splits into a few areas. You won't own all of it on day one. But this is the shape of it. **The outreach system** - Own the setup in Clay. That's the logic that finds the right people. It adds company data, writes custom lines, then routes each record to the right place. - Build the checks that keep the data clean. No repeats. No wasted credits. - Set up the exports. Records should flow into our outreach tools on their own. - Build the systems behind our shared inbox. **Notion** - Build and look after the databases. Clients, briefs, creative, creators, payments. - Set up the automations, views, and templates. The team then works from one clean system. - Move data in cleanly. Keep the naming the same throughout. **Reporting and data** - Build the pipelines so the numbers pull in clean. Spend, revenue, MER, aMER, and margin. They come fro ---------- ta, Google, and Shopify. - Look after the Looker Studio dashboards. And the connectors that feed them, like Windsor.ai or Supermetrics. - Automate the manual steps. No one should redo them by hand each week. The weekly Slack digest is one. **Automation across tools** - Build the "if this, then that" logic across Clay, Notion, Sheets, Slack, and the outreach tools. Use Zapier or Make. - Link the tools so data moves clean. And nothing gets typed in twice. **Keep it simple and clear** - Write short guides so each process can be re-done. It shouldn't live in one head. - Test things well before they go live. - Spot when a system is too big. Then make it smaller. --- ## The kind of person I want - You think in systems, not tasks. - You're at ease in tools you've never used. - You like the logic problem, not just the clicks. - You spot repeats, gaps, and mess that others miss. - You'd rather make a thing simpler than bigger. - You can explain how a system works in plain words. - You test before you trust. Read the example up top. Did you think "what's the key, where's the dedupe, how many tables is this"? Then you're the right type. --- ## Tools you'd work in You don't need all of these on day one. But this is the world you'd work in. - Clay, for lead data and routing - Notion, for databases and guides - Zapier or Make, for automation - Google Sheets and Looker Studio, for reporting. Plus a connector like Windsor.ai or Supermetrics. - Shopify, Meta, and Google Ads, to pull data. Not to buy media. Strong logic and the will to learn beat deep skill in one tool. --- ## The details - **Hours:** Starts part-time. Around 10 to 20 hours a week. There's more here than that, so there's real room to grow. - **Where:** Remote. I work with people across time zones. Where you are isn't the issue. Being reliable and clear is. - **Pay:** $5 an hour, based on skill. Or we agree a fixed price to build the core systems first. --- ## How to apply Don't send a long cover letter. Send me this. 1. A short note on a system you built or fixed. And what made it work. 2. One tool you'd never used, picked up, and got good with. 3. Your answer to this. The same company shows up as five rows in my list. How would you stop that? Keep it plain and simple. If you can think clear on that last one, we should talk.

title: Video Editor for Performance Ads Meta
job_title: Video Editor for Performance Ads Meta
description: ABOUT US We are a German Direct-to-Consumer supplement brand in the women's health space. Our entire creative workflow is AI-powered — from image generation to voice-overs to video clips. We produce high-performing direct-response ads for Meta and TikTok, targeting German-speaking women aged 35-55. (Brand name shared with shortlisted candidates.) THE OPPORTUNITY We are starting this role as PART TIME (around 20-30 hours per week). If you perform well during the first 4-8 weeks, we will upgrade you to FULL TIME with a higher monthly retainer. We are looking for a long-term editor, not a one-off freelancer. Our top performer can become our lead video editor and grow with the brand. WHAT YOU WILL EDIT 60 to 180 second talking-head ads in UGC and authority style. Each ad combines: - AI-generated video clips (Kling 3.0, Veo 3.1) - AI-generated still images (NanoBanana Pro) that you will animate - ElevenLabs voice-overs (in German — you do NOT need to speak German) - Medical 3D visualizations - Occasional real stock footage All edited together in CapCut Pro. REQUIRED HARD SKILLS - Advanced CapCut Pro: keyframe animations, slide-in/pop-up overlays, multi-track editing with 5+ tracks simultaneously (talking head, B-roll, visuals, text overlays, audio, music) - Voice-over-driven cutting: every cut must land precisely on the spoken word. The voice-over sets the rhythm, NOT the music. This is critical. - Subtitle creation and styling: bold, colored, animated, with key words highlighted in a different color. Subtitles must never cover the face or important visuals. - Text overlays for hooks, benefit callouts, and CTAs — cleanly animated in and out, on-brand - Infographic card overlays flown in over talking-head clips (e.g., a card showing what each herb does, or a comparison table) - Color correction and color grading to make AI-generated clips visually consistent. AI clips often have slightly different color temperature, saturation, and exposure — you must match them so the final video looks like it came from one source. - Audio mixing: voice-over loud and clear in the foreground, background music subtle (15-20% of voice-over volume), clean crossfades, no hard audio cuts - Export in 9:16 (1080x1920) for Meta/TikTok, plus 1:1 versions when requested REQUIRED UNDERSTANDING - Direct-response ad structure: Hook, Problem, Agitation, Mechanism, Product Reveal, Social Proof, CTA. You don't need to write this — but when editing you must FEEL where each section starts and ends and match the visual rhythm to it. - Pacing and cut rhythm: the hook (first 3 seconds) needs fast cuts and visual surprise. The mechanism explanation needs slower cuts so information lands. The CTA needs calm and clarity. You must master this fast/slow alternation. - Talking head ? B-roll switching every 3-8 seconds. Talking head builds trust, B-roll proves or visualizes what is being said. - Handling AI-generated clips: clips sometimes have artifacts, weird first/last frames, imperfect lip-sync, unnatural hand movements. You must know how to hide these issues — trim first/last frames, use cutaways to B-roll at the right ---------- nt, light cropping/ repositioning, smart transitions. - Scroll-stopping hooks: the first 3 seconds d ---------- whether someone keeps watching or scrolls away. You must be able to cut multiple hook variations of the same ad for A/B testing. - Audience awareness: our target is women 35-55, NOT Gen-Z TikTok users. The aesthetic is warm, trustworthy, mature — NOT loud, flashy, or Gen-Z. This is critical and most editors get it wrong. NICE TO HAVE - After Effects or DaVinci Resolve experience for animated infographics, particle effects, kinetic typography - Experience with Meta Ads Creative — knowledge of Hook Rate, Hold Rate, Thumb-Stop Ratio - Split-testing experience (different hooks, CTAs, visual styles) - Experience editing health, wellness, or supplement-style ads with a professional but not clinical look WHAT YOU WILL RECEIVE FROM US - Numbered clips (Clip 1 to Clip 46 etc.) - Full ad copy as a text document - Timing per clip with clear labels (talking head vs visual/B-roll) - Final voice-over as audio file - Mood references / example videos - Brand colors, fonts, and logo files WHAT YOU DELIVER The fully edited video with subtitles, text overlays, music, and infographic overlays — export-ready in 9:16 (and 1:1 when requested). WORK VOLUME & EXPECTATIONS - Multiple new ads per week - Fast turnarounds — first rough cut within 24-48 hours - Heavy iteration — you will often be asked to cut 3 different hooks for the same ad, change a CTA, or swap a scene. This is NOT criticism, this is performance marketing. Editors who take iteration personally will not work here. - Creative freedom within structure: copy and clip order are fixed, but transitions, zoom levels, text animations, and music choice are yours. GROWTH PATH - Weeks 1-2: Paid trial period (1-2 ads to evaluate fit) - Weeks 3-8: Part-time collaboration, building rhythm together - Month 2+: If output and quality are strong, upgrade to full-time position with higher monthly pay and lead editor responsibilities LANGUAGE NOTE The ads are in German, but you do NOT need to speak German. Subtitles will be reviewed by a German native speaker on our team. You only need to copy-paste subtitles correctly from the script we provide. HOW TO APPLY Please send: 1. Portfolio link (Google Drive, Vimeo, or website) — ideally with at least 2 examples of direct-response or UGC-style ads you have edited 2. Short answer (3-5 sentences) on this question: "When you receive an AI-generated talking head clip with a weird first frame and slightly off lip-sync, how do you handle it?" 3. Your CapCut Pro experience (months/years) and whether you also use After Effects or DaVinci 4. Your available hours per week and time zone 5. Your rate (per hour OR per finished ad — your choice) Applications without a portfolio will not be reviewed.

description: Management Accountant, Financial Dashboard Build (Short-term Project) About the role: We are looking for an experienced management accountant to join us on a short-term project (4-6 weeks) to build a live financial dashboard and supporting management accounts for a DTC ecommerce client. This is a hands-on build role. You will be designing and delivering a daily financial dashboard that pulls data from multiple sources via APIs (Zapier, Airtable, Shopify, Meta Ads, bank feeds), presenting estimated and actual figures with variance reporting across revenue, cost of goods, advertising spend, staff costs and overheads. The dashboard needs to work on a rolling daily basis, with data refreshing within 24-48 hours of the source transactions. You will be working under the direction of the Finance Director who will provide the data sets, access credentials and the overall structure. Your job is to take that brief and build the thing, working largely independently on the technical delivery. What you will be building The first deliverable is a daily financial dashboard with the following characteristics: (a) High-level summary rows for revenue, cost of goods, gross profit, expenses, VAT and net profit, with drill-down capability into subcategories (advertising by channel, COGS by supplier, staff costs by source). (b) Three-column structure per day: Estimate, Actual and Variance, with favourable/unfavourable variance logic built in. (c) Dual views: an accruals-based dashboard and a cash-based dashboard. (d) Populated initially with estimated costs (COGS from supplier invoices, staff costs from historical data, ad spend from recent actuals), then progressively replaced with live data as the API integrations come online. (e) Connected via Zapier (or similar) to Shopify (UK, US and ROW stores), Meta Ads, TikTok Shop, Stripe, PayPal, Revolut, Wise, Remote and Airtable (creator contracts), pulling actuals automatically. (f) Built with scalability in mind. The client is expanding into a group structure (multiple brands and entities), so the dashboard needs to be designed in a way that can be replicated and consolidated across additional businesses in the near future. Following the dashboard build, you will assist with Xero integration work: aligning the chart of accounts, reconciling recent months and ensuring the management accounts output ties back to the dashboard figures. What we need from you Essential: You are a qualified or part-qualified management accountant (CIMA or equivalent) with demonstrable experience building financial dashboards and management accounts from scratch, not just maintaining existing ones. You are comfortable working with AI tools and using them in your workflow. This is not optional. We use Claude, ChatGPT and similar tools as part of our delivery process and expect you to do the same. You have hands-on experience with API-driven data pipelines, whether through Zapier or direct API work. You need to be able to connect data sources, map fields and troubleshoot when feeds break. You have experience with Xero (or a comparable cloud accounting platform) and understand how to structure a chart of accounts for ecommerce businesses with multi-channel, multi-currency revenue. You can work independently with minimal supervision once given the brief and access. Preferred: Experience designing management accounts and dashboards for ecommerce, DTC or Shopify-based businesses. Familiarity with A2X, Finaloop or similar ecommerce accounting connectors. Experience building financial models that can scale across a company group (consolidated reporting, intercompany, multi-entity). Understanding of contribution margin, MER (marketing efficiency ratio) and channel-level unit economics. Practical details This is a remote, freelance contract. Hours are approximately 20 to 30 per week for an initial 4-week period, with the possibility of extending to 6 weeks depending on progress. Rate is $8-15 per hour Depending on Experience. There is potential for this to develop into a longer-term management accountant role as the client's group structure grows, but the immediate need is the project build. (b) A brief summary of a financial dashboard or management accounts pack you have built from scratch, including what tools and data sources were involved. (c) Your experience with Zapier or similar API/automation tools. (d) Your accounting qualifications and level. (e) Your availability to start (ideally within the next week).

description: Reports to: Owner | Hours: Full-time, several hours of daily overlap with US Mountain Time | Location: Remote (see region note below) About the role I co-own a lean local-SEO and digital marketing agency. We keep the team small on purpose. I handle client accounts directly and a group of VAs handles fulfillment. The problem this hire solves is me: I run too much of the business out of my own head and inbox, and things slip. I need someone who owns the day-to-day flow of communication and follow-through so I can stay on the work that needs me. This is not a task-taker role waiting for instructions. I want someone who watches the business, sees what is about to fall through a crack, and closes it before I notice it was open. What you'll own Inbox and email Triage my inbox daily. Flag what needs me, handle what doesn't, and draft replies in my voice for anything routine or client-facing. I should open my email to a short queue of decisions, not a wall of unread mail. Calendar and scheduling Own my calendar end to end. Book calls, protect focus blocks, handle reschedules, and make sure I am never the reason a meeting didn't get set. Send me a clear look at the day each morning and the week each Monday. Client communication and follow-ups Keep client conversations moving. Track every open thread, send proactive updates, chase the replies I owe people, and make sure nothing goes quiet. This is the single biggest source of stress for me today, so it is the most important part of the job. No client should ever email asking "any update?" because the update already went out. Delegating and QA on VA work Hand tasks to the VAs, confirm they understood the brief, and check the work before it reaches me or a client. You work alongside the VAs at an equal level, not above them. Think of yourself as the person who makes sure work actually gets finished to standard, not the person who assigns chores. Who you'll work with You report to me directly and work daily alongside our existing VAs. Most coordination happens over WhatsApp and ---------- . You won't manage the VAs, but you will rely on them and they will rely on you, so being easy to work with matters as much as being good at the work. Requirements Fluent, natural written English. You will draft client-facing email , so your writing has to read like a sharp American professional wrote it, not a translation. Several hours of real-time overlap with US Mountain Time, every working day. Proven experience as an EA, VA, or operations coordinator, ideally supporting a business owner or a small agency. Comfortable living in email , calendars, and a project tool day to day. We use ---------- and WhatsApp. Self-directed. You can take a vague request, figure out the intent, and run it down without three rounds of clarifying questions. Discreet. You will see client details, finances, and personal scheduling. Region note The overlap requirement shapes where to hire from. Latin America (Mexico, Colombia, Argentina, and similar) overlaps Mountain Time through a normal workday and is the cleanest fit. The Philippines works well if the person takes an evening or night shift on their end. Eastern Europe and most of Asia struggle to hit several hours of daily overlap, so weigh that before interviewing candidates from those regions. Nice to have Familiarity with local SEO, Google Business Profile, or digital marketing agencies. Experience drafting client updates and reports. A track record staying with one employer for a multi-year stretch. What success looks like I want to measure this hire by how much quieter my own head gets, so here is what "working" means at three checkpoints. By day 30 My inbox runs on a daily triage rhythm and I no longer scroll through everything myself. My calendar is fully in your hands and I have stopped booking my own meetings. You know every active client and the state of every open thread. By day 60 Clients get proactive updates from us before they think to ask. The "any update?" email has stopped arriving. You hand tasks to VAs and QA the output, and I see finished work instead of work in progress. I can go a full day without being the bottleneck on a routine decision. By day 90 I trust you to catch dropped balls before I do, and you catch most of them. I spend my time on client strategy and growth, not on chasing follow-ups and logistics. The background stress of "what am I forgetting?" is mostly gone, because you are holding it. Ongoing signals of a great fit Nothing client-facing goes quiet for more than a day without a reason I know about. I rarely repeat instructions, because you remember how I like things and apply it next time. You surface problems early with a proposed fix, not just a flag. When I'm out or heads-down, the business keeps moving without me.

description: We're Counter, a high-protein frozen food brand in the US. Our TikToks are real college students doing street interviews: handing strangers our food and filming their reactions. PAY $10 to $15 per finished video, paid weekly through Wise or Payoneer. Viral bonus on top when one of your edits hits big views in its first week. Honest heads up: this is a brand new program, so the first few weeks will be a little bumpy while we dial it in together. HOW TO APPLY (we skip anyone who skips this) 1. Start your reply with the word FREEZE so we know you read this. 2. Send 2 or 3 links to short vertical videos you edited, street-interview or reaction style. One line each on what you did. 3. Integrating AI/LLM capabilities throughout the product — not bolted-on chat widgets, but intelligent features woven into the user experience (triage, analysis, recommendations, natural language querying, content generation) - Working with the Google Ads, Meta Ads, and analytics APIs to ingest, normalise, and surface advertising data - Building CRM-style interfaces — database views, saved filters, inline actions, dynamic tables, drag-and-drop workflows - Developing the page/funnel builder module with overlay and popup elements - Implementing a consent management layer and data-triggered qualification rules - Writing clean, testable code against Gherkin acceptance criteria provided in each spec - Using Claude Code, Cursor, or equivalent AI-assisted development tooling as a core part of your workflow — not occasionally, but as standard practice - Shipping iteratively with a bias toward working software over perfect abstractions ## What We're Looking For - Strong production experience with Next.js 14+ (App Router, not Pages Router) — this is non-negotiable - Proven ability to build with LLM APIs (Anthropic, OpenAI, or similar) — prompt engineering, structured outputs, tool use, streaming responses, RAG patterns - Comfortable across the full stack: React/TypeScript on the front end, Node.js/serverless on the back end, PostgreSQL or equivalent relational database - Experience integrating third-party APIs — particularly ad platforms, CRMs, or data-heavy SaaS integrations - Ability to work from a detailed spec and translate user stories and business logic into shipped features without requiring architectural hand-holding - Familiarity with AI-assisted development workflows (Claude Code, Cursor, Copilot, Windsurf, or similar) and the discipline to review and own what the tools produce - Test-driven mindset — you understand Gherkin acceptance criteria and write code that satisfies them - Clean component architecture, sensible state management, and an instinct for UI that feels fast and responsive - Self-directed and reliable in a remote, async-first environment — you ship, you communicate, you don't disappear ## Tech Environment - Next.js (App Router), React, TypeScript - Tailwind CSS - PostgreSQL - description: We're a boutique email marketing agency building world-class Klaviyo programs for Shopify brands in fashion, spirits, jewelry, and beyond. We're small, fast, and obsessive about craft. We're looking for a senior email copywriter who'll rewrite a subject line twenty times, then cut a line they love because it doesn't sound like the brand. What you'll do: Own the words for multiple brands: concepting, writing, and shipping email and SMS copy that gets designed, built in Klaviyo, and sent to hundreds of thousands of subscribers. Subject lines, preview text, body copy, CTAs, all of it. Every week you move between brand worlds. High-end modest fashion one hour, premium whisky the next, streetwear after lunch. Each one has its own voice, and you switch between them without missing a beat. You'll work with our designers and strategists to turn briefs into email s that stop the scroll and move revenue. And the more you show us, the more you shape. The best writers here don't just write to the brief, they help d ---------- what the brief should be: the angle, the offer, the calendar, the strategy behind the send. How it works: This is a per-account role. You're paid per account you own, and the better you do, the more accounts you get. There's no ceiling. Deliver, and you keep earning more. How far this goes is up to you. Who we're looking for: • 3+ years writing email copy, specifically. Not "I write, and some of it was email ." Real campaigns, real results, real revenue. You know the medium cold: the subject line, the preview text, the first line, scannability, the CTA, and how copy maps to a Klaviyo block structure. • Native-level English on the page. Not just correct, but idiom, rhythm, and the instinct for when to break a rule. You write English that sounds like a person, not a translation and not a textbook. • A body of work that makes us jealous. Voice, rhythm, restraint, taste. Your email s read like someone wrote them for a brand they love, not like a template and not like a prompt. • You're a voice chameleon. You can sound like premium whisky in the morning and streetwear by lunch, and neither one sounds like you. Brand voice isn't a vibe you approximate. It's something you nail, every time. • AI is already in your toolkit, and you've figured out how to use it without sounding like it. Claude, ChatGPT, whatever sharpens your thinking and speeds up your drafts. But you'd never let an "elevate," an "unleash," or an "in a world where" slip into a send. You know the difference between AI that makes you faster and AI that makes you generic, and you only ship the first kind. If you're scared of AI, or addicted to its first draft, this isn't the role. • You understand email as a discipline, not just a writing assignment. You know what a flow is, why segmentation changes what you write, and how the offer and the angle move revenue. Bonus points if you can build the strategy, not just write to it. • You get design. You write with the layout in mind: how copy breaks across blocks, where the eye lands, what the headline does next to the hero. You'll push back on a layout that fights the words instead of just filling it in. • You overlap with Israel hours. Wherever you're based, your workday meets ours. This one is non-negotiable. We move fast and need you in the room, even when the room is Slack. Why it's worth it: • Your words ship, unwatered. We're small enough that nothing dies in committee. What you write Monday is in inboxes by Friday. • Brands worth writing for. Our clients care how they sound. No "just make it pop" briefs, no "add three more exclamation points," and a body of work you'll be proud of. • Direct feedback, fast growth. We tell you what's working and what isn't. No politics, no guessing where you stand. We live by five values: Unreasonable Hospitality, Design + Details, Extreme Ownership, Relentlessly Resourceful, and Clarity is King. If reading those made you nod, we should talk. If they made you roll your eyes, we won't. How to apply There's one way in: our Google form: ----------

THE KIND OF PERSON I REALLY NEED ----------------------------------------------------- You don't need to know everything already. But you do need to know how to find things out. When you hit something you've not done before, I need someone who has a sensible go at working it out — checking a help page, searching properly, looking at a previous example, or using an AI tool like ChatGPT or Claude to think it through — then has a careful attempt and flags anything they're not sure of. I'm glad if you use AI to get yourself unstuck — it's how good people work now. What I don't want is someone who goes quiet, guesses blindly, or waits for every answer to be handed to them. >> I don't need someone who knows everything. I need someone who knows how to find out. (One small thing that isn't in the form's list of questions: somewhere in your voice message, please also tell me what the temperature is where you are right now.) THE BOOKKEEPING SIDE, HONESTLY ---------------------------------------------------- It's light to start with — mostly posting invoices into Xero and keeping records tidy. You don't need years of bookkeeping behind you, and you don't need to be an expert. What I need is the common sense to have a go, think it through, and ask a good question when something's genuinely unclear. I'd far rather have someone who thinks clearly and flags a sensible question than someone who guesses and makes a mess. The bookkeeping will grow over time, with support from self-learning and your team — so there's room to learn built into the role. (And while we're talking ledgers: when you reach the application form, type the word ledger into box 7.) WHO YOU'LL BE WORKING WITH ---------------------------------------------- A small, personal team — me (Fiona), my husband Rudi, who looks after systems and tech behind the scenes, and our senior accountant in the Philippines. We work from home. It's personal, hands-on, and real. You'll be PA to me, but your day-to-day will run mostly through Rudi — systems, email s, onboarding, admin and process work — with bookkeeping guided by either myself, Rudi or eventually our senior accountant. The point of this role is to protect my time, keep work moving, and make sure important things don't get missed. You won't be just a number here — we're a small team, and we care about the people who work with us. WHAT YOU'LL DO ------------------------- • Help manage my email s and diary • Communicate with clients to get information in and keep work on track • Track follow-ups and chase missing records, answers, documents and approvals • Help with client onboarding • Draft email replies and client messages • Keep client records, folders and checklists tidy • Help move work in the door, through the process, and out the door • Support social media admin and post scheduling • Support general practice admin and help document repeat processes • Post invoices into Xero and support basic bookkeeping tasks • Take written instructions and voice notes and turn them into clear action • Spot problems early and flag them clearly • And anything else really that we need help with when it's needed This isn't an advisory role — you won't give accounting or tax advice to clients. But it is a communication-heavy PA role, so you'll need to be confident, clear, professional and comfortable dealing with clients to get things sorted. MUST-HAVES ------------------- • Strong PA, admin, operations or client-support experience • Experience supporting a business owner directly • Experience working remotely for a UK business, UK clients, or similar overseas clients • Excellent written and spoken English • Strong attention to detail and very strong organisation • Good spreadsheet skills, and confidence with email , online systems and shared folders (Gmail, Google Drive) • Some hands-on exposure to bookkeeping and/or Xero — you don't need to be experienced, but you should have actually used them. Xero certification would be a huge bonus. • Able to follow written and verbal instructions properly, and comfortable turning voice notes into action • Able to use initiative, work things out sensibly, and ask good questions when stuck • Able to take ownership without needing constant chasing • Reliable, trustworthy and professional • A modern laptop or PC, reliable internet, and a quiet place to work HELPFUL, BUT NOT ESSENTIAL -------------------------------------------- • Experience in a UK bookkeeping or accountancy practice • Experience with client onboarding or chasing client information • Experience with social media admin or post scheduling You do need to be switched on, organised, confident, and able to think. HOW WE'LL ASSESS YOU ----------------------------------- This is a serious role, so we'll assess properly. We'll be looking at your written and spoken English, your clarity of communication, your ability to follow instructions, your organisation and attention to detail, your ability to think and work things out, and your ability to take ownership and follow through. Please only apply if you're confident in those areas. PAY & CONTRACTOR TERMS --------------------------------------- • Pay is Php60,000 per month • This is an independent contractor role, not employment • Paid monthly in PHP — you handle your own taxes and contributions in the Philippines • Bring-your-own-device: we don't provide hardware initially • Full contractor terms will be set out clearly before work begins HOURS ----------- Full-time, based around UK time. We don't expect silly hours, but we need reliable overlap each weekday for communication, handovers and keeping work moving — typically 8:00am–12:00 noon UK time, which means late afternoon/evening in the Philippines depending on the time of year. We don't use invasive screen-tracking software. We manage by trust, communication and output. WHY THIS MIGHT BE THE PLACE FOR YOU ----------------------------------------------------------- I built this business so I could be there for my daughters. Family matters to me, trust matters to me, and doing good work properly matters to me — and I want the right person in this role to have that same dignity: to work from home, be trusted, do meaningful work, and grow with a small team that values good people. We're not for everyone. But if you're organised, reliable, switched on, and looking for a serious long-term role with a small UK firm, this could be a very good fit. Your job is to bring order to that: take things off the plate, build the systems that keep the business running, and turn loose goals into finished work. When there's no playbook, you research it, figure out the smartest way to do it, talk it through with the founders, build the process, and then act on it. A real example of what we mean: "We need to bring on a video editor. Figure out where to find good ones, what it should cost, screen the candidates, bring me your top picks, and once we approve, get them onboarded and working." That's the level of ownership we're after. We want to hand you a goal and trust it's handled, not assign you a checklist. If you bring problems wrapped in solutions instead of just questions, you'll thrive here. If you need step-by-step instructions for everything, this isn't the fit. We'll have a short check-in call once a day during the initial period to stay aligned, get you up to speed on how we work, unblock you quickly, and move quickly together. **What you'll do** It varies week to week, but expect a mix of: - Building SOPs and systems: Turning the things we do into clean, written, repeatable processes so the business runs more smoothly over time. The specific tools and tasks are learnable, and we'll teach you what's specific to us. What we can't teach is the resourcefulness and drive to own the outcome. **Who you are** - Resourceful: When you hit something you don't know, you figure it out. You research, you learn, and you come back with a plan, not just a question. - Proactive and ownership-driven: You anticipate what's needed, follow through without reminders, and treat the business as if it were your own. - Organized and systems-minded: You think in processes and checklists. You like building order out of chaos and enjoy finding smarter ways to do things. - Comfortable with ambiguity: A sharp, fast learner who can take a vague goal and find the path forward. - An excellent communicator: in written and spoken English, clear, professional, and easy to work with. You'll talk to the founders directly and represent us with vendors and contractors. - Hungry, with high standards and a strong work ethic: This matters to us more than your résumé. You take pride in your work, and you don't cut corners. - Honest, discreet, and trustworthy: You'll handle sensitive information. **Nice to have** These are bonuses, not requirements. One step: Record a short Loom or YouTube video** (a few minutes, on your own time) telling us: - A quick introduction about yourself and your relevant experience - Do you have any experience with video games? About the Role: We are a U.S.-based real estate law firm looking for a detail-oriented, organized, and proactive legal assistant to support residential real estate transactions from contract to closing. This is not a brokerage transaction coordinator role, listing coordinator role, lead management role, cold-calling role, or general real estate VA role. We are looking for someone who understands real estate transactions and can work in a legal environment, including attorney review, inspection deadlines, title coordination, lender coordination, closing preparation, client communication, document organization, and attorney escalation. Main Responsibilities: - Open and set up new real estate matters - Review contracts and email s to identify key transaction details - Enter and update client, agent, lender, attorney, and title company contact information - Track key dates, deadlines, and missing information - Coordinate with real estate agents, lenders, title companies, opposing counsel, and clients - Prepare standard documents and email s using templates - Organize email s, documents, and matter files - Follow up on missing information or pending items - Prepare files for attorney review - Flag unusual, unclear, urgent, or non-standard issues for the attorney - Support closing preparation and post-closing follow-up - Maintain task lists and update matter status clearly Experience We Are Looking For Strong candidates will have experience with some of the following: - U.S. residential real estate transactions - Contract-to-closing coordination - Buyer-side and/or seller-side transaction support - Real estate law firm support - Real estate transaction coordination - Title company, escrow, mortgage, or brokerage transaction support - Attorney review process - Inspection deadlines - Lender coordination - Title coordination - HOA or condo document requests - Closing preparation - Closing statements or settlement statements - Real estate document organization Experience with Illinois residential real estate transactions is a plus, but not required. Tools and Systems Experience with these tools is helpful, but not required: - Microsoft Outlook - Microsoft Teams - Microsoft To Do - Microsoft SharePoint or OneDrive - Smokeball, Clio, Odoo, or similar practice management systems - Adobe Acrobat - E-signature platforms - Real estate transaction management systems You do not need to know every system before starting, but you must be comfortable learning new tools and following detailed SOPs. This Role Is a Good Fit If You Are: - Able to think in context, not just complete isolated tasks - Very organized - Detail-oriented - Careful with deadlines - Comfortable following written instructions and SOPs - Able to communicate clearly in writing - Proactive about asking good questions - Able to notice when something needs attorney review - Comfortable working with many email s, documents, deadlines, and exceptions - Reliable, consistent, and accountable - Calm under pressure - Interested in long-term work with a small professional team - Impeccable written and spoken English This Role Is Not a Good Fit If: - Your real estate experience is mainly brokerage support, listing coordination, showing coordination, lead generation, CRM updates, social media, cold calling, or agent admin - You are looking for a general real estate VA role rather than a legal-support role inside a law firm - You are hoping this role is mostly posting listings, updating CRMs, or making things look nice in Canva - You have worked around real estate transactions but have not been responsible for contract-to-closing file coordination - You treat each instruction as a separate task without considering the full status of the matter - You only have general admin or data entry experience - You have never worked with U.S. real estate transactions - Your legal experience is mainly with local court filings, municipal courts, litigation, criminal matters, family law, immigration, or court-based legal work outside the U.S. - You have general legal experience but no direct experience with U.S. residential real estate transactions - Your real estate experience is limited to property research, data entry, lead generation, cold calling, or CRM updates - You need constant reminders about what to do next - You are uncomfortable reading contracts, email s, and transaction documents - You are not detail-oriented - You do not like documenting your work clearly - You struggle to follow multi-step processes - You prefer simple repetitive tasks with no judgment involved - You believe “I did not know” is a good replacement for asking a clear question - You think this job posting is too long to read carefully Important Expectation: > This role requires initiative, context, and judgment. > The best real estate transaction coordinators do not treat each instruction as an isolated task. They constantly ask: What is the status of this matter, what has already happened, and what needs to happen next without creating confusion, duplication, or risk? For example, before sending a document, a strong coordinator should think through whether the document is complete, whether it is the correct version, who needs to receive it, whether it has already been sent, whether it is meant for internal or external use, and whether sending it could create a deadline, legal issue, duplicate file, or client confusion. You will not be expected to provide legal advice. However, you will be expected to understand the context of the matter, notice when something is missing, unusual, unclear, urgent, or outside the normal process, and flag those items for attorney review. For example, a strong tea ---------- mber should be able to notice when: - The contract is missing the buyer’s attorney information - The inspection deadline appears to be tomorrow - The title company contact is not listed - The client’s phone number is missing - A transaction appears to involve a condo or HOA - An issue should be flagged for attorney review How to Apply: Please send your resume, a link to your OnlineJobs.ph profile, and a cover letter answering the questions below to ---------- A short summary of your experience with U.S. residential real estate transactions - Have you supported buyer-side transactions, seller-side transactions, both? - Describe one U.S. residential real estate transaction you personally supported from contract to closing - What stages did you handle? - Who did you coordinate with? - What documents or deadlines were involved? - What were you personally responsible for? - What real estate, legal, title, mortgage, or transaction management tools have you used? - What is your availability in U.S. Central Time? - What is your expected hourly rate or monthly salary? You will assist with monitoring LinkedIn profiles, maintaining campaign trackers, coordinating profile-related issues, updating records, and supporting general operational and administrative tasks. title: Content Writer (Fully Remote)
description: About This Position High Vibe PR is a boutique communications firm for companies and brands redefining the future of culture and technology. We've launched a $275M gaming fund, positioned platforms as the leaders in in-game UGC, and built thought leadership for some of the sharpest founders in AI and frontier tech. We're hiring a Content Writer based in the Philippines. This is a fully remote, 40-hour-a-week role. This is a writing role at its core. You'll produce blog posts, thought leadership, and listicles that earn attention and actually rank. While we use AI for ideation and edits, we are looking for a writer that creates copy that reads like a smart human wrote it, not a content mill. We care about substance and search in equal measure, and we're looking for someone who can deliver both. Does a strong hook and a headline that actually makes someone click get you excited? Can you take a dense, technical topic and turn it into something a busy founder wants to read to the end? Do you know your way around SEO, keywords, structure, search intent, without letting it flatten your voice? Do you have experience creating content for different types of formats? If that sounds like you, let's talk. Responsibilities I. Content - Write blog posts, thought leadership bylines, and listicles for clients across AI, frontier tech, and gaming - Apply SEO best practices — keyword research, search intent, structure, internal linking — so our content gets found - Research industries, trends, and writers deeply enough to write with authority on each client's space - Match the voice of each client and executive you're writing for, from punchy founder takes to measured CMO bylines - Edit and proofread your own work to a publish-ready standard, and help raise the bar on everyone else's - Track content performance and use what you learn to make the next piece better II. Collaboration - Support High Vibe's own content and thought leadership across the blog, LinkedIn, and beyond Requirements - 7–10 years of professional content writing experience - Strong SEO background, with a track record of content that ranks and converts - Excellent, native-level written English - Located in the Philippines - Sharp eye for detail and a genuine interest in PR Nice to Have (Not Required) - B2B writing experience, especially in the PR space - GEO (Generative Engine Optimization) experience — or the curiosity to learn it. This is the emerging discipline of getting brands surfaced inside LLMs, and it's a growing part of what we do. If you don't know it yet but want to, that counts. About High Vibe PR High Vibe PR is a boutique communications firm for companies and brands that redefine the future of culture and entertainment. As a small (but mighty!) team, we act as an extension of our clients' teams and as a trusted advisor. We work with a small number of clients so we can go deeper with each one and do work that provides real value. Our work goes beyond traditional PR to shape stories that create impact and define brands as industry standouts. What We Offer In charge of your own destiny. We're a small team — we don't play politics, aren't buried in bureaucracy, and have agency over our schedules. No assholes. Life's too short for oversized egos. When we evaluate clients, we first ask whether they're someone we want to work with every day. Unique opportunities. From a team off-site in Bali to VIP tickets at the Eras Tour, we know how to mix work with incredible experiences. Fully remote. Work where you're comfortable and productive, whether that's your living room or your favorite cozy café. To Apply - Send a cover letter to ---------- that includes: - A quick rundown of your writing tech stack and workflow - the tools you use to research, draft, optimize, and edit (AI or otherwise), and how they fit together - Links to two or three writing samples you're proud of (blog posts, bylines, or listicles) - Content you ranked on Google and a brief share on how you did it - Your favorite ---------- of 2026

title: Service Desk Manager (MSP)

Develop, implement, and enforce standardized service desk processes and workflows - Analyze ticket trends, recurring issues, and inefficiencies to recommend improvements - Drive adoption of best practices for ticket handling, communication, and documentation - Conduct regular check-ins to ensure alignment and address operational challenges - Foster a culture of accountability, efficiency, and continuous improvement Performance Monitoring & Reporting - Track and report on key metrics (SLA compliance, ticket volume, resolution time, backlog) - Use data to identify performance gaps and improvement opportunities - Provide regular operational updates to leadership Client Experience - Ensure consistent, professional communication with customers throughout ticket lifecycle - Address escalated concerns and ensure positive outcomes - Maintain high customer satisfaction through reliable and predictable service delivery QUALIFICATIONS Required - 3+ years of experience in a service desk, help desk, or MSP environment - Proven experience managing workflows, ticket queues, or service operations - Strong organizational and process management skills - Experience assigning and coordinating work across a technical team - Excellent communication and follow-up discipline - Ability to prioritize effectively in a fast-paced environment Preferred - Experience in an MSP or multi-client support environment - Familiarity with PSA/tools (Synchro PSA) - Clients receive timely, predictable service and communication

We also do SEO, social media, copywriting, and most things digital marketing or website related. Website project management is a high attention to detail role. You cannot fake attention to detail, you either have it, or you don’t. Don’t waste your time or ours if that’s not you. From when a new client comes on board, to the briefing, data collation and tracking, guidance with the client for the layout and website functionality, and then through to design concepts, and then onto tasking and liaising with the design and build team for the actual build and implementation. This is a marketing ideas role, and a communication role requiring good interpersonal skills. EG: In a recent simple project the client had 3 primary services, hats, shirts and badges. In the design layout and function briefing it was d ---------- we were to create 3 primary ‘doorway’ buttons on one row on the homepage linking to those product pages. Was it going to be in the client’s best interest? Should that page have the same priority as the 3 main product pages? What would your response have been to that client’s request? We have broken the website build process into 10 distinct stages, from project setup and client onboarding right through to design and build and onto quality assurance, a clear ‘go live’ process and handover steps to project completion rap up. We have a local tech, who handles the phones, helps in support and also does our SEO. We have another local tech, who handles the hosting, website version updates, managed support and all things WordPress for clients. We have several designers and web build dev’s who handles the design concepts, and the actual build as such. We also have a remote marketing person, who is our CRM specialist on the team. There is also a content marketing and social media specialist. So, is that you? Remember, don’t theorise about this! Website project management is a high attention to detail role. You cannot fake attention to detail, you either have it, or you don’t. Don’t waste your time or ours if that’s not you.

title: Outbound Sales Specialist (GoHighlevel|  Remote)
description: **GHL Closer – Remote** We're looking for a proven cold sales closer with real hands-on experience using GoHighLevel (GHL) and its CRM. You'll contact U.S.-based small businesses to introduce our GHL-powered automation services, demo the platform live, and close the deal. This role is on an as-needed basis. You will be informed before the start of each month whether your services are needed for that month. **Work Schedule** Monday to Friday 4 hours per day, between 10:30 AM and 4:30 PM EST **Compensation: Base + Commission** Guaranteed Monthly Base — $100/month, paid when you complete and document at least 50 sales calls to 50 different prospective businesses that month, where you spoke with a real person at the business — calls that reach voi cemail , an automated message, or any other non-human response do not count toward the 50. Proof required: timestamped call recordings (or CRM call logs with timestamps and contact names) for each of the 50 qualifying calls, submitted at month-end for verification before payout. Commission — 10% of the total deal value on every client you close. Commission for a sale is paid out after the client has remained active for 1 full month from their sign-up date. If the client cancels or churns before completing that first month, no commission is paid on that sale. Volume Bonus (Residual Commission) — the more you close in a single month, the longer you keep earning that 10% on the same client's revenue going forward: - 25–49 closes in a month: 10% for 1 additional month (2 months of commission total) - 50–74 closes in a month: 10% for 2 additional months (3 months total) - 75–100 closes in a month: 10% for 3 additional months (4 months total) - 100+ closes in a month: capped at 3 additional months — same as the 75–100 tier If a client downgrades or reduces their payment below the level at which the original sale was closed, the residual commission will be recalculated to be commensurate with the new (lower) payment amount, from that point forward. If a client cancels entirely, commission stops immediately for that client — no further commission is paid for that month or any subsequent month. **Requirements** - Excellent spoken and written English — non-negotiable - Real hands-on experience with GoHighLevel and its CRM tools — non-negotiable - Proven track record in outbound or cold sales - Comfortable running live product demos for prospects - Reliable internet connection and a quiet workspace - Comfortable making outbound calls, sending email s, and managing follow-ups **Preferred (not required)** - Experience building websites or funnels inside GoHighLevel - A portfolio of completed GHL websites/snapshots, if you have one **Responsibilities** - Contact small businesses that could benefit from our automation services. Leads will be provided — you're also welcome to bring and work your own leads alongside them. - Use GHL CRM to manage your pipeline and log every call and outcome - Run live demos of our GHL automation setup for interested prospects using the demo environment we provide - Explain automation features, handle objections, and qualify prospects - Close the deal, assist the client with signing the contract, and help them complete payment - Act as the client's point of contact for issue escalations during their first month under contract, helping resolve concerns or routing them to the right tea ---------- mber **What We Provide** - A steady flow of leads to work, in addition to any leads you source yourself - A pre-built GHL demo environment so you can walk prospects through real features live on calls - Generic talking points and a demo script covering key automation features, common objections, and pricing framing — you'll personalize it to each prospect - Ongoing support as you ramp up We're looking for someone consistent, confident, and motivated to grow with us long-term as volume increases. **To Apply** Send a short voice recording introducing yourself, and cover: your GoHighLevel experience, your outbound/cold sales background, your comfort level running live product demos, and (if applicable) a link to your GHL website portfolio.
